correctness.rationale: For any integer q≥2 the generalized binomial is a single integer power of q, so integrality is equivalent to a nonnegative exponent. At width m the exponent at zero-based position j is G(m)-d(m,j), with d(m,j) the number of gaps in (j,j+m]. Binomidness requires the initial length-L sum of d to be at least every shifted length-L sum. The Frobenius bound follows by reflecting nongaps in [0,F] into gaps; checking candidate gaps through 5 by rejecting any sum of two positive nongaps gives exactly the eight lists. When m≥F the sequence d(m,j) decreases; when L≥F the initial block contains the full nonnegative support; and when s≥F the shifted sum is zero. I independently checked the other 172 inequalities by updating the sliding gap-window sums. All pass, including the noninterlaced <3,4> case. Shapiro's Definition 4 and Proposition 9/Corollary 10 support the all-level and pyramid interpretation. In the finding, 'fails closure under adding two' means precisely failure of positive-index closure n∈S implies n+2∈S for n≥1, as required by the divisibility criterion; it is not a claim of closure of the finite gap set or a condition at n=0. value.rationale: The genus filtration gives a natural boundary in an existing all-level integrality question. The smallest semigroup outside the two-interlaced criterion is an actual positive instance at every width and index. The conductor reduction turns this bounded family into a result on infinitely many pyramid entries, rather than an empirical small-index extension or an exercise reproducing the seven covered cases. No claim about larger genus or the general ComboSum question is justified.
